summary.text: 什 is traditionally analyzed as 人 plus 十 and associated with a unit of ten, though 人’s precise contribution is unresolved. In 什麼, a separate account traces the spelling to reuse of 甚 for an interrogative word; its relation to the ten-unit use is unestablished.

formation.text: The reported 人+十 analysis is associated with a group or unit of ten, but does not settle the formal formation type or 人’s precise contribution. Although supplied Baxter–Sagart notations match for 什 and 十, the sources do not establish that 十 functioned phonetically in the original graph.

components.text: 人 is included in the traditional 人+十 analysis. Its precise contribution to the ten-unit sense is unresolved.
十 contributes the number ten in the traditional analysis associated with a group or unit of ten. The accounts do not assign it a phonetic role.

history.text: The received graph is traditionally explained as 人 plus 十. A modern rendering in seal-script style shows this arrangement, but it is not a dated artifact and does not establish the graph’s earliest form or development.

For interrogative use, a separate account says 甚 was reused to write interrogative words and 什 became another spelling. This is a whole-character spelling history, not a change to the original 人+十 graph; the proposed sound basis for reusing 甚 is not independently demonstrated.

uncertainties.text: The ten-unit association is supported, but the formal formation type and 人’s contribution remain unsettled. Matching supplied reconstructions for 什 and 十 do not by themselves establish a phonetic role for 十.

The early literary example has no established physical-witness date. The interrogative spelling transition is undated, and the recorded miscellaneous and other uses cannot be ordered into a semantic sequence from these examples.

senses.period: dating unresolved; early literary use cited
senses.text: A cited early literary passage uses 什 for a group organized in tens. The date of a surviving manuscript witness is not established.
Dictionary entries record 什 with the value 十, but their examples do not establish when this use began.
什 is also recorded with miscellaneous and things-related senses. The examples do not show how these relate to the ten-unit sense.

senses.period: Tang-Song onward in the cited account; transition dating unresolved

limitations.text: The early literary use supports the ten-unit sense, but no physical-witness date is established. The entries do not securely order the other recorded senses or demonstrate semantic links among them.
The interrogative spelling account gives no dated transition and does not establish a historical sound relation between the interrogative word and the ten-unit use.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The entry says the basic sense is “taking ten as a unit,” quotes the Shuowen account “相什保也。从人、十,” and cites *Zuo zhuan*, Duke Zhao year 1: “以什共車，必克.” It also reports a later use of 什 as 十 and an interrogative use from Tang-Song onward. This supports an analysis of the graph as 人 plus 十 associated with a group of ten, while Shuowen’s wording remains a historical explanation rather than independent proof of the formation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭「什」

evidence.text: The entry gives the fanqie 是執 and classifies the reading as voiced retroflex sibilant, entering tone, third division, rhyme category 侵/緝. Its displayed Mandarin reading includes shén and another reading whose tone marks are image-rendered. It does not identify 十 as a phonetic component; the cited Shuowen analysis assigns the graph components 人 and 十 without a phonetic/semantic split.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭「什」

evidence.source: 中國哲學書電子化計劃 (Chinese Text Project)
evidence.text: A search result for the primary text gives the passage “以什共車必克.” The database entry cited by CUHK associates this with the sense of organizing ten together. The passage is an early textual attestation, but no date for the composition or surviving manuscript witness is established by the pages inspected here; do not treat the traditional chapter date as the physical date of the text.
evidence.title: 春秋左傳：昭公元年 — 中國哲學書電子化計劃

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: This entry treats 什 as a variant of 甚 specifically in interrogative use. It says 甚 had an earlier meaning glossed “尤安樂,” was later borrowed for interrogative words such as 甚麼, and 什 became a spelling used for that interrogative use. This gives a distinct whole-graph borrowing/spelling history for the interrogative use; it is not evidence that 什 originated as a phonetic component in its original 人+十 graph.
evidence.title: A02621-008 什 (甚) — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry says 什 can be a partial variant of 甚 only in interrogative use. It reports that 甚 was borrowed for interrogative forms such as 甚麼 and that 什 was also used to write that use. The entry does not establish a date for the transition or independently demonstrate the sound resemblance underlying the account.

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry records the Shuowen explanation 相什保也。从人、十, with fanqie 是執. It gives the ten-unit sense and cites 管子: 十家為什，五家為伍. It also lists poem-section and miscellaneous senses, but the list does not establish their chronology or semantic links.

evidence.field: 字形; 《說文》; 形義通解; 《廣韻》; 中古音
evidence.text: The entry displays 什 with a 人十 component code and a small-seal image, but no bronze or oracle-bone form. It quotes Shuowen’s “相什保也。从人、十,” describes the basic sense as a unit of ten, and cites the Zuo zhuan passage “以什共車，必克.” It also lists later use equal to 十 and an interrogative-pronoun use in Tang-Song and later literary examples. Guangyun gives 是執; the displayed Middle Chinese categories are voiced retroflex sibilant, entering tone, third division, 侵/緝. The entry does not identify 十 as a phonetic component.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭「什」

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 甚 entry: pronunciation, meanings, variant forms
evidence.text: The entry gives 甚 the modern readings shèn, shén, and shé; under shén it lists interrogative and indefinite uses in 甚麼 and says that form is also written 什麼. Its cited literary examples include Ming and later works; these examples do not date the origin of the spelling.
evidence.title: [A02621] 甚 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 張雙慶, CUHK Centre for Chinese Linguistics Research Centre
evidence.field: 語文論析: 什麼／甚麼 pronunciation and writing discussion
evidence.text: The study argues that 什 was used to write the colloquial interrogative word in Tang-Song times and discusses how the 什 reading in 什麼 may have been affected by the following 麼. It notes a sound relationship between 什 and 甚 readings in the interrogative word, but this is a distinct account from the original ten-unit graph. The article’s proposed account is not itself a dated physical witness, and its pronunciation discussion does not establish the sound of the ten-unit word as the source of the interrogative word.
evidence.title: 語文論析: 「什麼」與「甚麼」相關討論

The 什 and 十 match in this system, which may be compatible with a phonetic relationship, but by itself does not demonstrate that 十 was phonetic in the original graph.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: No inspectable dated oracle-bone, bronze, or manuscript glyph image for 什 was obtained. The earliest graphic attestation and any possible corruption or regularization therefore remain unresolved.

The formation 人 + 十 is reported by Shuowen and accepted in the specialist dictionary’s account, but the sources inspected do not independently demonstrate whether the graph is formally associative, whether either element had a phonetic role, or the precise semantic relation of 人 to 十.

The dossier's assertion that 十 is phonetic conflicts with the accessible Shuowen-based explanation, which gives the components but does not assign 十 a phonetic role. No independent historical sound comparison for 十 and 什 was established; no phonetic-component claim should be made on this evidence.
The antiquity and exact manuscript dating of the cited *Zuo zhuan* passage were not established by inspected source pages. Its sense is an early textual use, not a securely dated physical witness.

The later senses “miscellaneous,” “utensils/things,” and Japanese readings were not independently traced to dated attestations here; do not order the dossier’s glosses into a chronology from dictionary lists.

Current Mandarin U+4EC0 record and the official Unihan click-through were unavailable. No verified official Unihan records for 人 or 十 were inspected, and no component-versus-host current reading array is supplied.

The provided Baxter–Sagart row only covers 什, not 十. Because the upstream table page was not verifiably opened in this turn, the local row is identified as packet data rather than external evidence; its notation should not be merged with other reconstruction systems.
No evidence supports a bulk local extract recommendation. The consulted character-specific references are cited as pages; reuse terms for extracting a repeatable corpus were not investigated.
No inspectable, dated oracle-bone, bronze, or manuscript form for 什 was retrieved. Earliest graphic attestation and possible graphic corruption or regularization remain unresolved.

The sources give 人+十 and associate the graph with ten-person or ten-unit organization; they do not independently establish the formal formation type or whether either component was phonetic. The dossier’s 十-phonetic claim is unsupported by the inspected references.

The left-zhuan passage is an early literary attestation, but no page inspected establishes the date of a physical witness. Dictionary gloss order does not establish chronology among ten, 十, poem-section, miscellaneous, or interrogative uses.

For interrogative 什, the MOE account gives a 甚 spelling/borrowing explanation, but the inspected pages do not establish an early dated attestation of either source-word use or the spelling transition.

No full external component-versus-host reading comparison was established. The supplied Baxter–Sagart row for 什 is packet data only and no 十 row was supplied; official Unicode Unihan pages for 什 and 十 could not be inspected.

No historical glyph image is proposed because exact Commons image pages could not be inspected and no alternate source established both image identity and reuse provenance. The Commons search result’s modern Qin-slip-style vector description is a lead only, not an ancient artifact image.
No bulk extract is recommended: reuse terms and editorial value for a repeatable corpus were not established.
No new inspectable dated early glyph or physical manuscript witness was found; earliest graphic attestation, graphic changes, and possible corruption remain unresolved.

The MOE account supports separate interrogative graph reuse involving 甚 and 什, but does not date the borrowing/spelling transition or establish the source word’s pronunciation independently. Do not infer it from a reconstruction of the ten-unit 什.
The cited 人+十 account and ten-unit sense do not settle the formal formation type or prove 十 was phonetic. No independently verified sound comparison between 十 and 什 is established here.
Unihan official lookup pages for both 什 and 十 failed to open, so current official readings were not externally checked in this pass.

The exact 什 seal-style candidate is a modern vector reconstruction/redrawing in Shuowen style. No inspected page established a dated physical specimen for this form, and the earlier dossier’s reported missing early forms remain a limitation; the image should not be captioned as an ancient artifact photograph.

The dossier’s proposed 十 phonetic role remains disputed/unsupported in the inspected formation accounts. The supplied Baxter–Sagart rows show matching 什 / 十 MC and OC notations, but local rows alone do not prove phonetic function and the upstream table was not independently opened. Current Mandarin readings differ; Unihan per-character click-through records were inaccessible.

The interrogative spelling explanation is separately about writing an interrogative word with 什/甚. The cited article discusses contextual pronunciation effects in 什麼, but the original sound relationship to the ten-unit word is not independently established.

The meaning timeline remains limited: CUHK cites the Zuo zhuan ten-unit passage and Song-era interrogative example, but pages inspected do not establish dates of surviving manuscript witnesses. Dictionary gloss order does not prove when equal-to-ten or miscellaneous senses arose or how they relate semantically.
No bulk local extract is recommended: these sources’ exact-page evidence and rights do not establish permission or editorial value for copying a broader corpus.
